payload.statement: Solver validation gate for this session: the reduced-order transport solver reproduces published reentry-alumina benchmarks before any solver budget is spent on the scientific question (particle formation vs surface chemistry vs atmospheric processing for ClONO2+HCl activation, 15-30 km). Experiment = run_validation (~5 solver runs). Pass/fail criterion as defined by the tool: gate PASSES only if all_pass == true, i.e. every check returns pass == true: V1 (calibration, Maloney+2025 JGR: 20-40 Gg Al2O3 at 10-30 km for 10 Gg/yr), V2 (held out, Maloney+2025: reaches ozone-layer altitudes in 1-3 yr with circulation), V3 (held out, qualitative, Maloney+2025: larger aerosol gives smaller stratospheric burden), V4 (held out, Ferreira+2024 GRL: ~30 yr for 4 nm particles by sedimentation alone), N1 (numerics: burden / input flux = mean residence time, positive and finite). Note: V1 is a calibration target (w_lstrat tuned to it), so only V2-V4 and N1 are independent evidence.
payload.prediction: all_pass == true, with all five checks passing. Expected values (from prior ledger entry 19f763a92b46f6ce, so this is a reproducibility check, not a blind prediction): V1 ~24 Gg (inside 20-40 Gg); V2 t10 ~1.0 yr, t50 ~2.1 yr (inside 1-3 yr); V3 burden(100 nm) ~14 Gg < burden(10 nm) ~24 Gg; V4 sedimentation-only t10 ~22 yr, t50 ~65 yr (brackets ~30 yr); N1 mean residence time ~3.4 yr (positive, finite). Non-gating drift check: if all checks pass but any value differs from the prior ledger value by more than 5%, log it as solver/config drift and report it before the scientific steps.
payload.falsified_if: all_pass == false, i.e. any single check (V1, V2, V3, V4 or N1) returns pass == false, or run_validation errors or returns non-finite values. On failure: STOP THE LOOP. Record a 'gate failed' verdict, do not run Morris screening, compare_coating_models, rank_measurements or any other solver experiment, do not pre-register scientific hypotheses, and spend no more of the 15,000-run budget until transport/numerics are diagnosed and the gate is re-run and passes. Failure in N1 points to numerics, V1 to calibration, V2-V4 to transport physics.
payload.experiment: run_validation (solver validation gate: V1 calibration, V2-V4 held-out benchmarks, N1 mass-balance numerics); cost ~5 solver runs of the 15,000 session budget

payload.statement: Agent-generated counter-hypothesis (particle formation): with fresh Morris runs this session, the input with the largest mu* is a particle-formation input {r_med_nm, sigma_g, oxide_fraction}, not a surface-chemistry input {gamma_alu, theta_hcl, gamma_sulf} or an atmospheric-processing input {p_sep, tau_coat_days, w_meso_mm_s, w_lstrat_mm_s}. Deliberately contradicts last session's result (p_sep on top, ledger a223bc70b97728ce), which must not be reused as evidence. Definitions: P = max mu* over the particle-formation inputs; Q = max mu* over the other 7 inputs; SE_i = sigma_i / sqrt(8) (a conservative upper bound on the SE of mu*, because Var|EE| <= Var EE); D = P - Q; SE_D = sqrt(SE_P^2 + SE_Q^2).
payload.prediction: SUPPORTED if D > 2*SE_D, i.e. a particle-formation input is on top and the lead is resolved at r=8. Planner expectation, recorded and not part of the rule: last session had p_sep 3.06 (sigma 2.61) vs r_med 2.15 (sigma 0.80), so I expect the outcome to be INCONCLUSIVE or FALSIFIED, with p_sep's point estimate on top. Reported but not adjudicated: mu* summed per group (particle formation / surface chemistry / atmospheric processing). If any output is bit-identical to the previous session, flag it as a replay, not a re-measurement.
payload.falsified_if: FALSIFIED if D < -2*SE_D (a non-particle-formation input is on top and the lead is resolved). INCONCLUSIVE if |D| <= 2*SE_D: record 'top input not resolved at r=8 (trajectory cap)'. An inconclusive result neither confirms nor overturns last session's p_sep result and must not be reported as support for either side.

payload.statement: Agent-generated (structural): the choice of coating structure (kinetic vs instant vs none) is a first-order uncertainty in the upper tail of the reentry/background activation ratio but not at its center. Metrics over the three structures, from the same parameter samples: R50 = max/min of median activation_ratio_pct; R95 = max/min of p95 activation_ratio_pct.
payload.prediction: R50 < 2 AND R95 > 5. Pre-specified secondary analysis (interpretation only, no effect on the verdict): also report R50 and R95 for kinetic vs instant alone. If R95 > 5 only when 'none' is included, the conclusion must read 'the no-coating end-member drives the tail', not 'coating structure is first-order among plausible coating structures'. Planner expectation: last session gave R50 = 1.529/0.760 = 2.01 (right on the threshold) and R95 = 153.3/14.92 = 10.3, but kinetic/instant R95 was only 1.46. So I expect the tail part to hold, driven entirely by 'none', and the median part to be unresolved. Ratios are approximately insensitive to the unsourced al_ablated = 0.912 Gg/yr if activation scales with mass in every structure; absolute levels are not.
payload.falsified_if: FALSIFIED if R95 <= 5 (whatever R50 is), or if R50 > 2.35. SUPPORTED if R95 > 5 and R50 < 1.7. INCONCLUSIVE if R95 > 5 and 1.7 <= R50 <= 2.35. This band is about +/-0.07 dex, roughly the 1-sigma sampling resolution of a ratio of medians at n=600, so the median part is unresolved there.
